bug_54: perimeter was the boundary-PIXEL count, measuring a 45-deg boundary at 1/sqrt(2) of its length: circularity 1.27 for a perfect disk (true ~1.0), 1.62 for a 45-deg square. Fixed to the Freeman chain convention (ortho x1, diagonal x sqrt2) in both analyze_image and morphology_table.
bug_55: marker detection (dist == maximum_filter(dist, size=5)) fired on mid-ramp pixelation plateaus, so one convex 4:1 cell was Voronoi-split into 3 fragments. Fixed to true regional maxima by morphological reconstruction (dist-1 under mask dist).

verdict: VALIDATED with two real bugs fixed (BUG 54 perimeter estimator, BUG 55 marker over-split). Analytic shapes: disk circularity 1.27 -> 0.92 (chain convention), diamond 1.62 -> 0.84 (chain exact 56*sqrt2), square chain 76 exact; single 4:1 cell 3 -> 1 object; touching pair still splits to 2; Otsu matches an independent implementation exactly; 50 diagnostics present with spot recomputes exact; real BBBC001 counts track manual counters (Pearson reported) with honest undercount discussion and human-counter disagreement quantified.
